tool_definitions.name: forward
tool_definitions.description: forward a port of this sandbox to the user's machine, so a server started with the job tool can be opened in their browser

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: the TCP port inside the sandbox (for add and remove)

parameters.name: job_name
parameters.description: an optional associated job name; 1–10 characters from [a-z0-9-] (for add)

tool_definitions.name: job
tool_definitions.description: run a shell command in the background. For a server, bind a fixed port and pass it as `port`; the tool forwards that same number, reports the URL the user opens it at, and does not discover an ephemeral port. In an interactive session you will be notified automatically when it finishes; in a non-interactive session you will not.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the job name; for start, use one short role such as 'check', not a specific compound such as 'cachecheck'—a live duplicate is automatically numbered, such as 'check-1'; 1–10 characters from [a-z0-9-] (for all actions except 'list', 'prune')

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: an optional TCP port inside the sandbox to forward to the user (for start)

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: the job names to watch for wait

parameters.name: wait_for
parameters.description: whether wait returns after any or all watched jobs end

parameters.name: wait_seconds
parameters.description: how many seconds to wait at most — max 4m 30s (default)

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: the command line (for action 'start'); if omitted, re-runs previous job by name

parameters.name: intent
parameters.description: for action 'start', what you are doing, as a 5 to 7 word phrase opening with a capitalised -ing verb, such as "Regenerating every golden in the scratch copy"
